MSG_FIFO window (2kB range at 0x800) is a write-only message FIFO. Any write to this address range appends data to the FIFO. Internal hardware handles byte/word packing; the least significant 12 address bits are ignored. The FIFO's pass-through mode means that when the SHA engine is ready, write data passes through, keeping fifo_depth at 0 while fifo_empty toggles low for a cycle.

The last beat of the App data moves the state machine to append the encoded output length if the hashing operation is KMAC. The output length is the digest width, which is 256 bit always. The logic appends 0x020100 (little-endian) to the end of the message. The output data goes to MSG_FIFO. Because the MSG_FIFO handles un-aligned data inside, the KeyMgr interface logic sends the encoded output length value in a separate beat. After the encoded output length is pushed to the KMAC core, the interface logic issues a Process command to run the hashing logic.

The state machine inside the AppIntf logic starts when it receives the first valid data from any of the AppIntf. The AppIntf module chooses the winner based on the fixed priority. Then it forwards the selected App to the next stage. Because this logic sees the first valid data as an initiator, the Apps cannot run the hashing operation with an empty message.
